top.line: The homepage should be a daily, versioned vault edition
top.para: I would like a job at about 05:45 each morning to write a new homepage edition, with the homepage as a vault: every edition a signed commit with links, screenshot and release note, variants for A/B tests, and forks for other audiences. The agent built it locally; time goes in the vault API, 317 ms against 44.

in-short.line: Daily signed editions, served as plain files, load fast
in-short.para: A scheduled job writes an edition each morning. Each is a commit with a signed tag, links, screenshot and release note. Encrypted objects can sit on S3, a CDN or GitHub Pages. Locally, today's edition took 4 requests, yesterday's 3, and repeat loads none within two minutes. Variants, a stats lane and synthetic users complete it.

why.line: The page that most needs freshness changes least
why.para: Today the homepage regenerates only when the site is released, so it stands still when I do not publish. An edition would come each morning from a job reading the latest articles, wires and industry news, deciding what leads, follows and rotates out. The wire and full article list can stay live.

correction.line: Pages serves the site; the vault API is slow
correction.para: I had it wrong: newsroom.sgit.ai is served by GitHub Pages; the Lambda is the vault API the Industry Wire reads through. A cold wire load made eight sequential API requests of 360 to 810 ms, ending 3.9 seconds after the page. Warm medians were 317 ms against 44, and immutable objects lacked cache headers.

static.line: sgit already reads vaults from plain static files
static.para: sgit.ai cloned a vault in 65.4 seconds through the API and 2.63 seconds from plain GETs, twenty-five times faster, though the static host was local. The API is a convenience, not a requirement. Content-addressed objects cache for ever; only the ref must not. Static copies are frozen until re-exported, which suits a daily homepage.

demo.line: A local homepage vault loaded in four requests
demo.para: With sgit 0.21.0 an edition job wrote three editions, each committed and signed as home-v0.1.0 to v0.1.2. Exported as static files, today's edition loaded cold in 4 requests and 4.7 KB, repeat loads within two minutes in none, yesterday's in 3. Four chained requests: about 0.2 seconds static, 1.3 through the API.

sequence.line: Only the ref changes; everything else caches for ever
sequence.para: The shell and read key come from GitHub Pages. The ref names today's commit, the commit names the tree and the tree the page, so each step waits on the last. Only the ref is uncached. The browser decrypts and records the variant shown. The public read key cannot become write access.

history.line: Past homepages, variants and forks are one commit away
history.para: Each edition is a commit, so any day's homepage reopens exactly as it was, with links, screenshot and release note, and the job can rotate links fairly. Variants share a commit, making A/B tests a choice in the page. A fork gives another language, publisher or reader their own homepage.

stats.line: An append lane gathers stats; synthetic readers check daily
stats.para: A stats lane took 300 synthetic page-load beacons at 2.6 ms each, all read back; the click rates were invented. Beacons still need the API, and the 1,000 pending file cap means the morning job must collect and clear daily. Five to ten synthetic readers run each morning to spot breakage or slowdowns.

handled.line: Search snapshots, revocation and a mirror's reader need handling
handled.para: Search engines see an empty shell, so the shell should carry a plain snapshot of today's edition naming its commit, a projection rather than a copy. Bytes published into git stay in history, a reason to use S3. A mirror needs a reader first; the homepage is that reader.

brief.line: Build /front/ first and prove it before switching
brief.para: Build /front/ from the vault, leaving the homepage alone. Run the edition job at 05:45 UK time, export to S3 behind a CDN with immutable objects cached a year, add a shell with a search snapshot, history links, two variants and a stats lane, and daily synthetic users. Time it for two weeks; move the wire too.

limits.line: The demo was local and nothing is scheduled yet
limits.para: The demo used local servers and counts requests, not network time. Live timings come from one sandbox location, medians of ten requests. Beacons and clicks were synthetic. The morning job, S3 export and /front/ are proposals. With this site's traffic, A/B differences may take weeks to appear.

sources.line: Sources: sgit.ai's documentation on static hosting and lanes
sources.para: From my voice memo of 14 October 2026; the demo and timings were run by this site's agent that day, with quotes checked against sgit.ai's documentation: Take the API out of the path, Static hosting, Live vault docs, Surfaces, Credentials, Append lanes, vault telemetry and The mirror is gone.
